title_en: What Did You Say in Chinese

sentences.en: My friend and I are eating at a restaurant, and there are a lot of people inside — it's very noisy.
My friend is talking to me, but it's too noisy, and I don't hear him clearly.
I ask him: "What did you say?"
My friend says it again, but I still don't hear it clearly.
We walk outside the restaurant, where there aren't as many people.
My friend says it again, and this time I hear it clearly: "We're going to watch a movie tomorrow."

quiz.q: Why can't the narrator hear the friend clearly at first?
What does the narrator say when they don't catch the words?
What are the friend and narrator going to do tomorrow, according to what the narrator finally hears?

grammar.p: 你说什么？（asking someone to repeat what they said）
grammar.e: Use 你说什么？when you didn't catch the words themselves — different from 听不懂, which means you heard the words but didn't understand the meaning.
grammar.x: 我问他：“你说什么？”— I ask him: "What did you say?"

grammar.e: 清楚 means clear; 没听清楚 says the sound itself wasn't clear enough (too noisy, too far away) — not that the meaning was hard to understand.
grammar.x: 太吵，我没听清楚。— It was too noisy, and I didn't hear clearly.

grammar.p: 又 + verb（doing something again — already happened）
grammar.e: 又 describes a repeat of an action that has already taken place, unlike 再 which is for something not yet done.
grammar.x: 朋友又说了一次。— My friend said it again.
